newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen firms, but capped by price concerns.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen firms, but capped by price concerns.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures were slightly firmer at midday on Monday, but the topside was capped after Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita said there was concern about prices.

"There is a high possibility that the Japanese economy will continue to recover. We will see how the weak yen and improving supply-demand conditions will affect prices in Japan," Matsushita told a news conference this morning after Sunday's meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) industrial nations.
The December contract was at 98.97, up 0.01 from Friday's settlement. It moved between 98.94 and 98.97.
"BOJ governor Matsushita's comments made us hesitant to go long," said a dealer at a city bank.
"This is the second time after similar comments on prices last week," he said.
But aggressive selling was curbed as those who had expected complaints from abroad about Japan's current fiscal and monetary policies failed to sell, traders said.
Neither talks between President Clinton and Prime Minister Hashimoto nor among G7 nations over the weekend sought a change in Japan's low interest rate policy and its fiscal tightening.

Unless the market factors in a rate rise of a half a point by December, the December contract is unlikely to fall from the current level, traders said. It is at the level before the BOJ's "tankan" corporate survey showed weak business sentiment among non-manufacturers and small corporations.
"If the market believes there is a 0.5 point rise in the discount rate by December, the December may fall to 98.93. But we are not so sure about that," said another dealer.
Traders say the focus is on Japan's industrial output data for March, due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT), which includes the trade ministry's forecasts for April and May.
The key overnight call rate firmed to around 0.50 percent by midday as banks' fund-raising demand was solid ahead of the month-end, traders said.

The BOJ retained its accommodative credit stance on Monday. The central bank left the money market in surplus of an estimated 190 billion yen by refraining from its regular money market operation at 9.20 a.m. (0020 GMT).
The benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at an unchanged 0.56 percent in a small volume of 10 billion yen.--Risa Maeda, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3342-8570
